title: INT8 weight-only GPTQ/AWQ interop probe suite and telemetry anchors
creator: Priya Shah
description: We need a distinct probe suite to validate INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ) quantized model variants across the serving stack and to anchor telemetry to deterministic golden outputs. The goal is to detect subtle drift introduced by kernel swaps, alternate quant libs, sequence-length edge-cases, or batch/kv-cache interactions before they reach customers. This ticket scopes the integration harness, a small canonical prompt set (anchor prompts), and lightweight canary automation that runs on every runtime kernel change or quant-profile update.
acceptance_criteria: Probe harness runs end-to-end against at least 3 model families (small/med/large) producing anchor token-level hashes for GPTQ and AWQ variants.
Anchored telemetry records token-delta and perplexity diffs; alerts fire when delta > configured threshold for any model+kernel combination.
Canary job integrated into pre-merge CI for runtime kernel swaps and into nightly regression pipeline; failures block canary gates with clear rollback playbook.
Tests include sequence-length stress (8/128/2048), multi-batch convergence, and KV-cache warm/cold scenarios.
Documentation: Confluence runbook describing how to add new anchors, interpret metrics, and perform a rollback (links included).
Smoke PRs: 2 runtime PRs that demonstrate failure mode + automatic alert and one rollback execution recorded in incident notes.
Telemetry storage: anchor snapshots persisted in the quant-profiles registry and versioned with profile IDs.
Low overhead: the probe should add <5% to nightly CI runtime and be runnable locally by engineers with a single script.
test_plan: Harness: python-based probe that can load model variant, run anchor prompts, compute token-level normalized edit distance and log token hashes.
Data: canonical anchor set (200 prompts) mixing synthetic synthetic-edge cases, in-domain examples, and customer-like queries (anonymized).
Matrix: run permutations across kernels (cuda-optim, custom-opt, fallback), quant lib versions (GPTQ v1/v2, AWQ v1), and sequence lengths [8, 128, 2048].
Metrics: token-delta, normalized-lm-score, top-k distribution shift, and inference latency/cost delta per token.
Thresholds: token-delta > 0.5% or normalized-lm-score regression > 1.5% triggers FAIL; smaller regressions flagged for triage.
CI gates: lightweight canary per PR (fast subset of anchors) + nightly full sweep. Canary failures open ENG ticket and annotate originating PR/commit.
Golden fallback: if a runtime/kernel change fails, automatic fallback to last-known good kernel/model variant for dedicated capacity customers.
Chaos: manual chaos run to validate canary sensitivity (introduce a small weight perturbation and assert detection).

2026-03-12: Implemented telemetry exporters to Datadog: token-delta, nlm-regression, and alert rule drafts under monitors/quant-anchors. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4587

risks: Anchors could be overfit to a particular model family and miss regressions for others — mitigate by ensuring cross-family anchors and rotating anchor subsets.
Telemetry noise from non-deterministic kernels may create false positives — mitigate with repeated-run averaging and hashed token sequences.
Storage and privacy: anchors containing customer-like text must be sanitized/anonymized — compliance review required for any customer-derived anchors.
CI cost: full nightly sweep is expensive on large families; ensure throttling and use reserved test capacity during non-peak hours.
next_steps: Finish PR for full anchor sweep orchestration and merge the probe harness (owner: Liam).
Wire alert playbooks in Datadog and create a dedicated dashboard for anchor drift (owner: Observability team).
Run full nightly sweep against medium and large families and capture baseline snapshots (owner: Priya).
Coordinate with runtime team to add the canary job as a required check for kernel changes (owner: Runtime infra).
Prepare a short postmortem template to record any detection -> rollback flows observed during the initial 2 weeks.
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on determinism-friendly checks: token-hashes and normalized LM metrics rather than full human-eval scoring to keep CI cheap.
We will iterate on thresholds after 2 weeks of telemetry to reduce false positives; initial thresholds are conservative to prefer catching regressions.
If a kernel change causes >1% token-delta across >5% of anchors for a production model, automatic canary rollback is triggered for Dedicated customers as a safety measure.
